title: Personal Incident Postmortem Queue
dataSources: Life score (`lifeos:score`), quests / tasks (`quest:task`), habit streaks (`streak:status`), life achievements (`achievement:life`), household leaderboard (`household:leaderboard`), plus every other `index=personal` sourcetype as input.
app: The parody-the-enterprise meta layer — a Personal NOC (house-health wall), Personal SOC (entry / impossible-travel), Personal SRE (SLOs on your own habits), and a gamification layer (XP, achievements, streaks, household leaderboards) — all computed in Splunk over `index=personal`.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=lifeos:score incident_open=yes
| stats count as open_incidents, values(incident_type) as incident_types by domain
| sort - open_incidents
description: Tracks unresolved personal incidents that still need a retro, fix, or systems change.
value: Life-OS thinking is only useful if failures feed learning loops instead of vanishing after the week ends.
implementation: Mark unresolved incidents in `lifeos:score` and summarize open postmortem backlog by domain.
visualization: Table of domains with open incident postmortems.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks which personal failures or setbacks still need a real review instead of being forgotten.
